record_identity.title: ICE AI-assisted resume screening reportedly routed inexperienced recruits into shortened training

incident_identity.historical_event_name: ICE AI-assisted resume screening reportedly routed inexperienced recruits into shortened training
incident_identity.date_basis: NBC News reported the hiring and retraining issue on 14 January 2026; the underlying screening occurred during the preceding ICE hiring surge.

summary: During an ICE hiring surge, an AI-assisted résumé-screening process reportedly classified some inexperienced applicants as having law-enforcement experience and routed them into shortened training before manual review and retraining.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: NBC News reported, based on agency and source accounts, that résumé-screening output assigned law-enforcement experience to some applicants who lacked it. ICE manually reviewed the affected cases and directed additional training. The reviewed evidence does not establish that the recruits performed field duties without correction or caused public-safety harm.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: The workflow converted inferences from applicant materials into an experience designation that carried training-path authority. Manual review later corrected the designations, but only after the routing decision had been made.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: The occurrence shows why automated screening in high-consequence hiring must separate inferential signals from verified qualifications before those signals control training or deployment pathways.
assessment_boundaries: The principal independent report relies partly on unnamed sources and does not disclose the model, decision rule or complete number of affected recruits.
No reviewed evidence establishes downstream field harm or discriminatory allocation across protected groups.
